text:
alisha: Heads up — vendor pushed a chunk of our A100 shipment by ~3 weeks. We have to decide whether to: 1) stand up partial dedicated pools now, 2) delay activation until full delivery, or 3) accept staggered billing. Need input from infra + finance. cc @matt @sofia

matt: Oof. Do we know which racks/serials are delayed? can we choose which units they hold back?

alisha: They said it's the last 8 units from the PO — not specific serials yet. They offered partial delivery and said billing will be per-shipment unless we negotiate otherwise.

sofia: From billing side: cloud vendor charges will be per-unit per-hour once we activate. If vendor invoices us for hardware, that will be separate (capex). If we want pro-rata for Dedicated pools, we can delay activation on our side to avoid runtime charges. But that affects customers expecting capacity.

jordan: From ops, we can do partial activation: create two dedicated pool configs (pool-A / pool-B), tag them by vendor-shipment-id, and only advertise pool-A to routing. That buys time while keeping some capacity live. We can also set autoscale max to match actual hardware.

alisha: Nice. Does anyone see issues with routing + rollout if we create half pools? I want minimal work for the SRE oncall.

matt: Routing wise it's easy: add a routing policy that prefers pool-A, then pool-B fallback. We should add a canary rule for high-priority tenants. Example route snippet I used before:```json
{"route": "dedicated", "preferred_pools": ["pool-A"], "fallback": ["pool-B", "hosted"], "priority": "latency"}```

sofia: Also, we need to update billing tags so finance can map usage to the vendor invoice. If we spin up half the pool under the same billing account, pro-rata becomes harder. My suggestion: use a separate billing project/account for pool-B (delayed batch). Then finance-bot can reconcile per-project invoices.

finance-bot: FYI: creating a separate billing account will add overhead for monthly reconciliation but is doable. I'll approve a temporary project if infra creates it and tags resources with "vendor:shipment-42".

infra-bot: Quota check: current quota in us-west1 for A100-family GPUs is 120; partial activation (8 units) will not exceed quota if we retire 8 pre-prod units. Run `gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --format=json` to confirm region-level quota.

jordan: I'll handle the quota/retire flow. Plan: 1) create pool-A with available hardware (live), 2) reserve pool-B but don't advertise, 3) create billing project for pool-B, 4) route production to pool-A + hosted fallback, 5) re-run canary when remaining hardware arrives.

alisha: Sounds good. Can someone file the cloud quota increase / reserve request and link it here? We might need +20 GPUs for peak demo next month.

matt: Filed: https://console.cloud/requests/req-98765 — requested +20 GPUs in us-west1, reason: demo + burst. Made it high priority.

sofia: Thx — finance will watch that invoice path. Also please add me to the billing project once created.

jordan: I'll create the billing project and pool-B this afternoon, and retire 8 pre-prod units to free quota. Will ping once done.

alisha: Great — owners: Jordan (infra), Sofia (finance). Next sync if vendor confirms final shipping dates or if quota request is denied. :thumbsup:
